figures.title: Upstream STAR two-stage workflow
figures.caption: STAR first builds a reusable genome index, then maps reads and emits alignment and quantification products.
figures.alt_text: Flow diagram from FASTA and optional GTF through genomeGenerate to an index, then from FASTQ and the index through alignReads to SAM or BAM, junctions, logs, and counts.

figures.title: Upstream genomeGenerate algorithm
figures.caption: Genome generation packs the reference, constructs and packs the suffix array, builds SAindex, and optionally inserts annotated splice junctions.
figures.alt_text: Detailed genome generation flow with reference scan, forward and reverse genome, suffix prefix partitioning, sorting, packing, SAindex construction, optional junction insertion, and index publication.

figures.title: Upstream STAR read alignment algorithm
figures.caption: STAR serializes input-chunk parsing before workers search maximal mappable seed prefixes, cluster and stitch seeds, score transcripts, and emit alignments.
figures.alt_text: Read-alignment flow from a shared FASTQ stream through locked chunk parsing, then per-worker read encoding, maximal mappable prefix searches on both strands, seed collection, genomic windows, seed stitching, transcript scoring, multimapping selection, and output.

figures.title: Index and runtime data model
figures.caption: The base genome and packed suffix structures remain conventional STAR files; Overlay and Delta add validated BlackSTAR metadata and sparse inserted-reference structures.
figures.alt_text: Data model showing Genome, packed SA, SAindex, chromosome metadata, and gene tables in a base index, with optional Overlay full arrays or a Delta package containing added sequence, inserted suffixes, rank metadata, annotations, and identity manifest.

figures.title: Threading and memory map
figures.caption: BlackSTAR parallelizes dominant index stages and retains STAR's read-level alignment workers while adding conditional affinity recovery, adaptive record-safe chunks, and eligible private-load NUMA placement.
figures.alt_text: Threading and memory diagram separating coordinator, genome-generation workers, SAindex workers, junction workers, and read-alignment workers. The alignment path recovers the allowed CPU-place union when explicit OpenMP binding narrowed the spawning thread, serializes record parsing under the existing input mutex, dispatches adaptive one-megabyte chunks at high thread counts, and shares packed Genome, SA, and SAindex memory. Eligible private high-thread loads interleave pages while shared loads retain the default policy.

figures.title: Accepted BlackSTAR change map
figures.caption: Blackstar.2 combines the accepted deterministic index, persistent insertion, integrity, and deployment work from blackstar.1 with qualified affinity, dispatch, NUMA-placement, and transcript-recursion alignment improvements.
figures.alt_text: Side-by-side upstream and BlackSTAR modules with accepted additions highlighted for parallel index generation, Full Overlay Delta sequence insertion, package validation, atomic publication, release selection, alignment affinity recovery, adaptive high-thread input chunks, eligible private-genome NUMA interleave, and transcript-recursion copy elision. The normal STAR command and measured output interface is retained.

figures.title: Full-index benchmark
figures.caption: Across three order-balanced CHM13 pairs, BlackSTAR reduced mean genomeGenerate wall time by 49.48 percent while all 42 substantive index-file comparisons were byte-identical.
figures.alt_text: Benchmark diagram comparing stock STAR mean 1225.78 seconds with BlackSTAR mean 619.30 seconds across three paired runs, a 49.48 percent reduction and 1.98 times speedup, with 42 of 42 file comparisons byte-identical.

figures.title: Full, Overlay, and Delta insertion modes
figures.caption: Full writes a conventional complete index, Overlay reuses base files plus replacement structures, and Delta stores only the validated sparse addition.
figures.alt_text: Decision diagram from a base index plus named FASTA and optional GTF to Full, Overlay, or Delta output, comparing compatibility, artifact size, build work, and load behavior.

figures.title: Delta virtual suffix array
figures.caption: Delta preserves the base packed suffix array and merges sparse inserted suffix records logically at lookup time.
figures.alt_text: Virtual suffix-array diagram with a base packed SA, a small sorted set of inserted suffix records and rank positions, and a lookup function selecting either a base entry adjusted by inserted rank or an inserted entry.

figures.title: Atomic publication and integrity
figures.caption: BlackSTAR builds into a private staging directory, validates identity and completeness, then atomically publishes a complete artifact.
figures.alt_text: Publication state machine from inputs through private staging, checksums and manifest validation, fsync and atomic rename, then immutable complete artifact and checksum-pinned deployment selection, with failures quarantined.

figures.title: Qualified benchmark summary
figures.caption: Qualified evidence separates strong paired full-build timing, one-time Delta construction, descriptive Delta runtime cost, and correctness controls.
figures.alt_text: Evidence hierarchy showing paired full-build speedup as a qualified performance claim, Delta build time and package size as one-time measurements, runtime difference as descriptive due to fixed run order, and exact mapping controls.

figures.title: Correctness and release boundary
figures.caption: Blackstar.2 release acceptance combines build identity, sanitizers, alignment runtime safety, byte identity where formats are unchanged, mapping equivalence, adversarial rejection, paired performance, and deployment controls.
figures.alt_text: Release-gate diagram covering fork version and OpenMP identity, focused sanitizers, ordinary and inherited-binding alignment paths, private and shared genome loading, uncompressed and compressed reads, canonical BAM records, byte identity for conventional formats, mapping and count equivalence for BlackSTAR formats, corruption rejection, paired full-size performance, deployment rollback, and explicit exclusions.

figures.title: Accepted, rejected, and superseded work
figures.caption: The history ledger separates accepted blackstar.1 and blackstar.2 release work from rejected experiments, archived prototypes, and invalidated or superseded evidence.
figures.alt_text: Status lanes listing accepted release work for memory-adaptive index construction, bounded SAindex and junction work, Full Overlay Delta insertion, integrity and deployment gates, H01 affinity recovery, A02 adaptive chunks, A05 NUMA placement, A06 transcript recursion, and Q01 cumulative qualification. Separate lanes retain rejected prefork, libdeflate, A01, A02b, and A09 work, archived multi-sample and BAM-compression prototypes, and superseded benchmark evidence.

figures.title: Experimental roadmap
figures.caption: The roadmap traces blackstar.1 through accepted H01, A02, A05, and A06 work, rejected A02b and A09 alternatives, Q01 qualification, the blackstar.2 release, and later kernel and index experiments.
figures.alt_text: Gated roadmap from blackstar.1 through corrected A00, accepted H01 affinity recovery and A02 adaptive chunks, rejected A02b producer-consumer queue, accepted A05 NUMA-aware private loading and A06 transcript-recursion copy elision, rejected A09 LTO and PGO variants, passed Q01 cumulative qualification, and the qualified blackstar.2 release, followed by proposed alignment kernels, output, multi-sample, and index stages.

figures.title: A01 touched-window-bin reset
figures.caption: A01 correctly replaced full window-bin clears with sparse restoration, but its paired performance series inherited a one-core affinity failure; the effect size is invalidated and the source remains excluded.
figures.alt_text: Side-by-side flow diagram comparing the qualified release, which clears every slot in both window-bin arrays for each read, with excluded A01, which records each used bin and strand once and restores only those slots; correctness passed, but the performance effect is invalidated by inherited CPU affinity.

figures.title: A02 input-dispatch attribution
figures.caption: Corrected full-corpus A02 diagnostics measured 49.52 percent input-lock occupancy, 71.28 aggregate mapping concurrency, and a 12.93-second finish spread, selecting finer scheduling units for implementation.
figures.alt_text: Diagnostic flow from shared FASTQ streams through one input mutex, whole-chunk parsing, and private mapping, with 96 active workers, 49.52 percent input-lock occupancy, 71.28 equivalent mapping CPUs, and a 12.93-second finish spread leading to the selected finer-chunk path alongside parser, producer-consumer, and rollback alternatives.

figures.title: H01 alignment-affinity recovery
figures.caption: Accepted in blackstar.2, H01 restores the full CPU-place union before pthread creation when OpenMP binding is requested, recovering a 5.20-fold failure mode while passing ordinary-path noninferiority.
figures.alt_text: Three-lane diagram showing the qualified release inheriting one two-CPU OpenMP place across 96 pthread workers and taking 223.54 seconds, H01 restoring 48 places and 96 CPUs before worker creation and taking 43.00 seconds, and the ordinary unbound fast path producing 43.49 versus 43.48 second medians across five pairs.

figures.title: A02 adaptive input chunks
figures.caption: Accepted in blackstar.2, A02 uses 1 MB record-safe input chunks at 64 or more threads, reducing median full-corpus wall time by 13.41 percent uncompressed and 8.74 percent through zcat while lowering peak RSS.
figures.alt_text: Before-and-after alignment dispatch diagram showing H01 workers receiving 30 MB chunks with a long completion tail, A02 selecting 1 MB chunks at 64 or more threads while retaining legacy behavior below that boundary, and qualified results of 13.41 percent uncompressed and 8.74 percent gzip median gains, 6.77 percent lower peak RSS, six paired correctness passes, and a canonical BAM pass.

figures.title: A05 NUMA-aware private genome placement
figures.caption: Accepted in blackstar.2, A05 applies NUMA interleave to eligible high-thread private genome loads while preserving caller policies, reducing the exact 96-thread full-corpus median by 22.51 percent over A02 with unchanged measured outputs.
figures.alt_text: Attribution and before-after diagram showing the rejected A02b producer-consumer queue, A02 private genome pages undergoing automatic NUMA migration, A05 selecting interleave only for eligible default-policy private loads while preserving inherited bind and interleave subsets, and exact public evidence of a 74.01 to 57.35 second uncompressed median with all output comparisons passing; gzip timing is labeled supportive because control variability exceeded its gate.

figures.title: A06 transcript recursion copy elision
figures.caption: Accepted in blackstar.2, A06 forwards unchanged recursive transcript state by const reference and copies only mutating or terminal branches, reducing copy-constructor CPU by 35.97 percent and the five-pair full-corpus median by 2.29 percent with exact measured outputs.
figures.alt_text: Before-and-after recursive stitching diagram showing A05 copying transcript state on include, exclude, and terminal paths; A06 receiving a const reference, making a private copy only for include mutation or terminal finalization, and forwarding exclude state without copying; evidence shows copy CPU falling from 351.96 to 225.35 seconds, a five-pair median falling from 57.39 to 56.11 seconds, a positive paired interval, exact outputs, compressed-input support, a canonical BAM pass, and a clean end-to-end sanitizer run.

figures.title: A09 LTO and PGO evaluation
figures.caption: A09 independently tested LTO and full-corpus-trained PGO; both preserved exact measured outputs and reduced binary size, but five-pair median gains of 1.21 and 1.20 percent missed the 2 percent practical gate.
figures.alt_text: Two-branch toolchain evaluation from the cumulative H01, A02, A05, and A06 source. The LTO branch reduces binary size by 17.47 percent and improves the five-pair median from 55.75 to 55.32 seconds, a 1.21 percent gain. The PGO branch trains for 1 hour 20 minutes, reduces binary size by 22.15 percent, and improves the median from 55.89 to 55.20 seconds, a 1.20 percent gain. Both pass five of five output comparisons but are rejected below the 2 percent practical gate; a note explains that other builders must regenerate profiles for the exact source and compiler.

figures.title: Q01 cumulative alignment qualification
figures.caption: Q01 qualifies the cumulative H01, A02, A05, and A06 source promoted in blackstar.2 with 33.20 percent uncompressed and 28.54 percent compressed median paired full-corpus gains, exact outputs, safety checks, and reproducible packages.
figures.alt_text: Qualification diagram comparing qualified blackstar.1 with the H01, A02, A05, and A06 source promoted in blackstar.2. Replicated full-corpus tests show wall time falling from 84.28 to 56.17 seconds uncompressed and from 90.61 to 64.03 seconds through zcat. Shared-index BAM, inherited-affinity recovery, eight sanitizer scripts, 24 insertion checks, four SAindex checks, official upstream STAR compatibility, and two byte-identical qualification-package builds pass. The final state is accepted in blackstar.2.

figures.title: BlackSTAR 2.7.11b-blackstar.2 promotion
figures.caption: Blackstar.2 promotes the Q01-qualified H01, A02, A05, and A06 alignment stack on top of blackstar.1 while preserving protected-master CI, explicit exclusions, and a separate external-deployment boundary.
figures.alt_text: Promotion diagram from upstream STAR 2.7.11b to the qualified blackstar.1 index and insertion release, then through H01 affinity recovery, A02 adaptive input chunks, A05 NUMA-aware private loading, A06 transcript-recursion copy elision, and Q01 cumulative qualification. Replicated performance, exact-output safety, inherited insertion and SAindex compatibility, versioned release packaging, and protected-master build-and-test gates lead to the accepted blackstar.2 release boundary. A01, A02b, A09, alignReadsMulti, prefork workers, and threaded BAM compression remain excluded, and external deployment requires separate authorization.
